test_title: PYST 16: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - GA (Held On 28 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Alauddin Khilji's reign is marked by his successful defense against which foreign invader?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mongols**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alauddin Khilji**, who ruled the **Delhi Sultanate** from **1296 to 1316**, is celebrated in history for his successful defense of India against the **Mongol** invasions. The **Mongols** of the **Chagatai Khanate** launched several large-scale attacks during his reign, aiming to conquer the heart of North India.
 
• The major **Mongol** invasions occurred in **1297-98**, **1299**, **1303**, and **1305**. Unlike his predecessors, **Alauddin Khilji** adopted a proactive military stance, defeating the **Mongol** forces in battles such as the **Battle of Jalandhar (1298)** and the **Battle of Kili (1299)**. **Hence, the option Mongols is correct.**
 
• To protect the capital, **Delhi**, from **Mongol** raids, he constructed the **Siri Fort** around **1303**. This fort served as a massive defensive garrison and the second city of **Delhi**.
 
• **Alauddin Khilji** implemented rigorous military reforms to sustain a large army. He introduced the **Dagh** system (branding of horses) and the **Chehra** system (descriptive rolls of soldiers) to ensure the quality and loyalty of his troops.
 
• His **Market Control Policy** or **Price Control Measures** were specifically designed to keep the cost of living low, enabling him to maintain a massive standing army with relatively low salaries, which was essential for the continuous defense against **Mongol** threats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Timur (Tamerlane)**: He was a **Turco-Mongol** conqueror who invaded India much later, in the year **1398**. His invasion took place during the reign of **Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah Tughluq** of the **Tughlaq Dynasty**. **Timur** sacked **Delhi**, causing widespread destruction, but this was long after **Alauddin Khilji** had died. **Hence, the option Timur is incorrect.**
 
• **Babur**: He was the founder of the **Mughal Empire** in India. **Babur** invaded India in the **16th century** and defeated **Ibrahim Lodi** in the **First Battle of Panipat** in **1526**. His era is distinct from the **Khilji** period by over two centuries. **Hence, the option Babur is incorrect.**
 
• **Mahmud of Ghazni**: He was the ruler of the **Ghaznavid Empire** who conducted **17 raids** into India between **1000 and 1027 AD**. His primary motive was to plunder the wealth of Indian temples, such as the **Somnath Temple** in **1025 AD**. He predates the **Khilji Dynasty** by nearly 300 years. **Hence, the option Mahmud of Ghazni is incorrect.**
 
• **Khilji Dynasty**: It was the second dynasty to rule the **Delhi Sultanate**, founded by **Jalal-ud-din Firuz Khilji** in **1290**. **Alauddin Khilji** was the most powerful ruler of this dynasty, known for his administrative reforms and territorial expansions into **South India** under his general **Malik Kafur**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Zafar Khan**: He was one of **Alauddin Khilji**'s most valiant generals who played a crucial role in repelling the **Mongols**. He died heroically in the **Battle of Kili** in **1299** while fighting the forces of **Qutlugh Khwaja**.
 
• **Administrative Centralization**: To prevent internal rebellions while focusing on external **Mongol** threats, **Alauddin** prohibited the social gatherings of nobles and banned the use of wine and intoxicants.
 
• **Revenue Reforms**: He was the first Sultan to insist that in the **Doab** region, land revenue should be assessed on the basis of measuring the land (**Paimash**). This ensured a steady flow of income to the state to fund the military.
 
• **Economic Impact**: His strict enforcement of prices for grains, cloth, and other necessities ensured that even during **Mongol** sieges, the supply chain and economic stability of **Delhi** remained intact.
